title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: Education budget and ITMs
sections.summary: Over 600,000 students are enrolled in MOE-run or supported schools, with FY2020 Education expenditure budgeted at $13.3 billion, and 23 industries have developed ITMs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: More than 600,000 students are enrolled in the Ministry of Education (MOE)-run or supported schools, junior colleges and institutes of higher learning (IHLs).

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The financial year (FY) 2020 budgeted expenditure for Education is $13.3 billion, the third highest after Defence and Health no less.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On transformation of education, 23 industries in Singapore have developed their ITMs under the Future Economy Council.

sections.label: Education-related ITMs
sections.summary: Of the 23 ITMs, two relate to education: Early Childhood Education Sector and Adult Training and Education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Out of the 23 ITMs, the ones related to education are two – the Early Childhood Education Sector, and Adult Training and Education.

sections.label: Education Transformation Map team
sections.summary: The speaker urges Government to form a team to develop and articulate an Education Transformation Map for the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We need to bring on board more Singaporeans to help understand the aspirations, demands and challenges we face and will face.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge Government to put together a team to develop and articulate an Education Transformation Map for the future.

sections.label: Digital accessibility and literacy plans
sections.summary: The passage asks MOE's plans to strengthen digital accessibility and literacy and ensure equal access to devices, software and supervision for all students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What are MOE's plans to strengthen digital accessibility and literacy for all and to ensure every student has equal access to the hardware devices, the software applications and supervision, especially students in financially or socially challenged households, and especially students who are not in mainstream school settings, such as those in special schools or home-schooling settings?

sections.label: Extending SPED school years
sections.summary: For SPED students unlikely to proceed to open employment or further studies, MOE should consider extending school years to age 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One, for Special Education (SPED) school students who are unlikely to proceed to open employment or further studies, MOE should consider extending the current school years of SPED schools to age 21.

sections.label: SEN support and lifelong learning
sections.summary: The passage calls for MOE and stakeholders to address SEN support gaps, including IHL SEN funds, SkillsFuture inclusion and lifelong learning pathways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For instance, the SEN funds in IHLs are currently only limited to those with sensory disabilities – those who are visually impaired or deaf – and they are not extended currently to those with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), dyslexia or autism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For everyone with SEN, learning with the appropriate support should not stop after the formal school years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There are insufficient efforts to include the special needs workforce in the SkillsFuture movement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Neither is there enough envisioning of a lifelong learning pathway for this special group of learners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, call for a deeper dive by MOE and other key stakeholders, such as the major disability Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to address this important need.

sections.label: Admissions beyond exam results
sections.summary: Speaker urges MOE to consider aptitude tests and interviews for admissions instead of relying on exam results, so students and parents value learning interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Regardless of what MOE says, if assessments and tests are graded and counted as your overall results, students will continue to mug for these assessments and these tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I urge MOE to consider more options to admit students to their schools of choice; to their courses of studies instead of simply relying on their exam results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Consider relying on aptitude tests or interviews to ascertain a student's interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In this way, we will be better able to persuade students and parents that it is important to develop a child's interest in learning and enjoy acquiring knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This comes in the wake of other initiatives, such as the revamped Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) scoring this year onwards and enlarging aptitude-based admissions into tertiary institutions.

sections.label: SEEL scholarship to Singapore Polytechnic
sections.summary: With an inhouse scholarship from SEEL, he went to Singapore Polytechnic to pursue a diploma in telecommunication engineering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: With an inhouse scholarship from SEEL, he went to Singapore Polytechnic to pursue a diploma in telecommunication engineering.

sections.label: Replicating drive for lifelong learning
sections.summary: The concern is how to replicate their drive for lifelong learning in children in generally well-off times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The concern for us is how we can replicate their drive for lifelong learning in our children in these times when we are generally well-off.

sections.label: Full subject-based banding pilot
sections.summary: Speaker was encouraged by MOE's move towards full subject-based banding, piloted in 28 secondary schools this year, whose outcomes will inform rollout to all secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, last year, I spoke about how our education system can better cater to the unique strengths and interests of our students by providing more opportunities for differentiated learning, depending on the student's ability at a particular point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Now, I was encouraged by MOE's move towards full subject-based banding (FSBB) which, I understand, is being piloted in 28 secondary schools this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: The outcomes and the students' experiences in this pilot project will provide useful learning points as the Ministry finally rolls out FSBB to all secondary schools.

sections.label: UPLIFT taskforce progress update
sections.summary: UPLIFT was set up in October 2018 to help children from poorer backgrounds benefit from education, and the Minister is asked for an update after a year and a half.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: The Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce (UPLIFT) was set up in October 2018 to see how we can help address the challenges that children from poorer backgrounds face, so that they are able to benefit fully from our education system and go on to maximise their potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: As it has already been a year and a half since UPLIFT was set up, I would like to ask the Minister if he could provide an update on the work and progress of this task force.

sections.label: Bilingual to bicultural talents
sections.summary: Singapore's bilingual advantage is being tested, and the country has moved from nurturing bilingual talents to nurturing bicultural talents, signalling progress in its bilingual policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: However, with changes in the world and the global economy, Singapore's bilingual advantage is now being tested and challenged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We have now moved from nurturing bilingual talents to nurturing bicultural talents, and this signals progress in our bilingual policy.

sections.label: Encouraging Mandarin use among students
sections.summary: It asks how MOE can encourage students to learn, speak and use Mandarin more, noting PM Lee said more people speak Mandarin at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Several months ago, Prime Minister Lee said more and more people were speaking Mandarin at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: How can MOE encourage our students to learn, speak and use Mandarin more?

sections.label: Mother tongue and National Language learning
sections.summary: It asks whether more English at home affects mother tongue learning, how MOE can help proficiency, and suggests learning the National Language without exam pressure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: As more and more people speak English at home, is the learning of mother tongue adversely affected?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: How can MOE help students to become more proficient in learning mother tongue?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand that our school children have a great deal to learn already and we are concerned about their well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But, perhaps they could learn the National Language without the pressure of examinations.

sections.label: MOE changes to CCE delivery
sections.summary: It states MOE has made significant and impactful changes to how CCE is delivered, with the last review done in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MOE has made significant and impactful changes to the way we deliver CCE to our students, with the last review done in 2014.

sections.label: Mental health in CCE syllabus
sections.summary: It proposes that mental health and wellness issues be incorporated in the CCE syllabus, even at the primary school level.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, issues related to mental health and wellness should be incorporated in the CCE syllabus even at the primary school level.

sections.label: Hygiene and values during COVID-19
sections.summary: It states that amid the COVID-19 outbreak, lessons on personal hygiene and personal and community values shaping social responsibility should be incorporated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, in the midst of the current Coronavirus Disease of 2019 (COVID-19) outbreak, it is important to incorporate lessons on personal hygiene as well as personal and community values that shape social responsibility.

sections.label: Parental involvement in CCE
sections.summary: It states parents' values, beliefs and behaviours shape how children treat others, so parental involvement in teaching and learning CCE would enhance its value.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Parents' values, beliefs and behaviours will most certainly shape how their children treat others and how they behave towards others.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, parental involvement in the teaching and learning of CCE would enhance its value.

sections.label: CCE curriculum review update
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry for an update on the review and enhancements to the CCE curriculum to anchor children on strong moral values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry provide an update on the review and the enhancements that would be made to our CCE curriculum to ensure our children are anchored on strong moral values?

sections.label: IB Theory of Knowledge module
sections.summary: The passage states that the International Baccalaureate programme includes a Theory of Knowledge module.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The International Baccalaureate programme (IB) includes a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) module.

sections.label: TOK in secondary curriculum
sections.summary: The passage asks whether this is addressed in the secondary school curriculum and whether MOE is examining modules like the IB's TOK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As most of our students are not in the IB programme, I would like to ask if this is currently being addressed in our secondary school curriculum and, if so, in what ways?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And if MOE is examining modules like the IB's TOK to explore how we might enhance our teaching approaches in this regard.

sections.label: Semakau landfills running out
sections.summary: The passage says to educate them on the Semakau landfills that are running out in 2035, instead of 2045.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Let us educate them on the Semakau landfills that are running out in 2035, instead of 2045.

sections.label: CCE curriculum update since 2014
sections.summary: The passage asks MOE if there will be an update to the Character and Citizenship Curriculum since 2014 and what changes make CCE more relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to ask MOE if there will be an update to the Character and Citizenship Curriculum since it was last introduced in 2014 and, if so, what are the changes to make CCE more relevant.

sections.label: Youth suicide and mental health statistics
sections.summary: The passage states suicide is the leading cause of death for ages 10 to 29 and cites Singapore mental health and IMH help-seeking figures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Suicide is the leading cause of death for those who are aged between 10 and 29.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The second Singapore Mental Health Study by the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) released in 2018 reveals that one out of seven Singaporeans experiences a mental health condition in their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The number of young Singaporeans between the ages of 16 and 30 who sought help from IMH's community health assessment team from 2015 to 2017 has seen an increase of 190%.

sections.label: 70-70 Asia-Ready Exposure target
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced the "70-70" target for a new Asia-Ready Exposure Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced the "70-70" target for a new Asia-Ready Exposure Programme.

sections.label: Expanding students' regional language skills
sections.summary: It is necessary to expand students' language skills to include those of the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Most importantly, to support our students, it is necessary to expand their language skills to include those of the region.

sections.label: Support for Asia-Ready Exposure Programme
sections.summary: A speaker was glad Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced the "70-70" Asia-Ready Exposure Programme, believing more exposure helps students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And that stint of about one and a half months he actually did really well, and you can tell from the knowledge that he has gained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I was quite glad that Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced about the "70-70" Asia-Ready Exposure Programme because I believe that when we give more of our students more of those exposures, it would help them in future, not just in their career, but companies that operate in Singapore or Singapore companies that want to venture overseas.

sections.label: Global-ready Exposure Programme and through train
sections.summary: The Ministry of Trade and Industry has a Global-ready Exposure Programme involving internship, with a possible through train from Asia-ready to Global-ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Start them young right, but actually push them a bit further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I know that the Ministry of Trade and Industry has a Global-ready Exposure Programme and the Global-ready Exposure Programme was about internship and maybe offer a through train from Asia-ready to Global-ready; from cultural understanding to internship opportunities.

sections.label: Learning ASEAN languages for students
sections.summary: A speaker asked if the Ministry would extend to students the opportunity to learn ASEAN languages, noting current Third Language options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: To help our students take full advantage of these opportunities, I wonder if the Ministry is prepared to extend to students an opportunity to learn ASEAN languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Currently, the MOE Language Centre provides Malay (Special Programme) and Indonesian languages as Third Languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: These options are only open to students ranked in the top 10% of their PSLE cohort.

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund for Digital Readiness
sections.summary: Last year's Committee of Supply debates announced the Government would establish the "Our Singapore Fund for Digital Readiness".

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: In last year's Committee of Supply (COS) debates, it was announced that the Government would establish the "Our Singapore Fund for Digital Readiness", which aims to support community initiatives that promote digital readiness.

sections.label: MOE and NLB digital literacy
sections.summary: The speaker proposes MOE work with NLB, which runs the SURE programme and a Digital and Information Literacy Community of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Hence, they cannot be taught in silo and have to be contextualised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: I would further propose that MOE work closely with the National Library Board (NLB) which has, for several years, implemented its Source, Understand, Research, Evaluate (SURE) programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: NLB has extensive experience in the area of digital and information literacy and has recently set up a Digital and Information Literacy Community of Practice (DIL-CoP), which brings together academics, practitioners and experts in the area of digital and information literacy to share experience, theory and practice in strengthening policies, research, strategies and initiatives in the area.

sections.label: Devices and Internet access
sections.summary: The question asks how MOE will ensure students, particularly less privileged ones, have their own devices and ready Internet access.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: How will MOE ensure that our students can have their own technological devices and ready Internet access, particularly for students who come from less privileged backgrounds?

sections.label: Subsidies for lower-income students
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will consider additional subsidies for lower-income students to purchase devices.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider providing additional subsidies for students from lower-income families to purchase devices?

sections.label: ICT talent and graduates
sections.summary: The speaker describes hiring ICT talent and asks how many ICT graduates the six local universities produced in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: We have formed agile squads, hired data scientists, hired people with digital marketing skills, hired millennials with user experience or user interface skillsets, hired project managers that can manage the IT programmers that are based at the offshore development centres in India, Myanmar and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: We are hiring many infocomms or info-communications technology (ICT) talents but we cannot get enough local ICT talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: As we transform our economy to be digital-focused, we need our six local universities to produce more ICT talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to ask the Minister how many ICT graduates have our six local universities produced in the last three years.

sections.label: Youths aged 10 to 29
sections.summary: In 2018, the figures spiked to 94 youths between the ages of 10 and 29.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, the figures spiked to 94 youths between the ages of 10 and 29.

sections.label: IMH young people seeking help
sections.summary: IMH reported that young people seeking help jumped by 190% from 2015 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: IMH has reported that young people seeking help has jumped by 190% from 2015 to 2017.

sections.label: Mental health as secondary subject
sections.summary: Singapore's centralised education system lets MOE make basic psychological knowledge a secondary school subject in its own right.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is specially equipped to tackle this issue because we have a centralised education system and MOE can do so much more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It should not be just a topic in CCE or during the form teacher's guidance period, but a subject in its own right in secondary schools in which basic psychological knowledge can also be imparted so that young people can have the tools to understand what they might be going through.

sections.label: Teacher retooling and development courses
sections.summary: Shorter technology cycles and policy shifts require teachers to retool, and studies suggest less formal, more interactive development courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat highlighted in his Budget Statement this year that with shorter technology cycles, skills acquired need to be constantly refreshed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Also, the recent policy shifts in our education system, such as the "Learn for Life" initiative, will also require our teachers to undergo some level of retooling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: This is backed by empirical studies on teacher development going back 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: They instead suggest that the teacher development courses be structured less formally and allow for more interaction, collaboration, reflection and feedback among teachers to refine their skills.

sections.label: Next Bound of SkillsFuture initiatives
sections.summary: SkillsFuture initiatives include expanded Work-Study programmes, Queen Bee company partnerships, and NACE expansion to two more IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Among the specific initiatives under the Next Bound of SkillsFuture are the increased capacity of SkillsFuture Work-Study programmes; partnership with Queen Bee companies to better support training of potential and current hires; and the deepening of workplace learning capabilities, including the expansion of the National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning (NACE) to two more IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to find out more about the	plans	on	how	the	SkillsFuture	Work-Study programmes will be expanded; what are some Queen Bee companies that SkillsFuture Singapore will partner with; which two IHLs will be appointed to house the new NACEs; and what are the plans in expanding opportunities for workplace learning.

sections.label: SkillsFuture top-ups before 2025
sections.summary: SkillsFuture measures should motivate skills upgrading, with top-ups to be used before 2025, especially by those aged 40 to 60.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture measures should motivate them to beef up their skills, retool themselves and chart their own future careers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: This round of top-ups must be utilised before 2025, a condition that should signal urgency and spur many into action, especially those aged 40 to 60.

sections.label: Online SkillsFuture Career Guidance tool
sections.summary: Clear linkages are needed between jobs, skills and CET courses, with an online tool assessing competencies and directing individuals to courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: There should be clear linkages between job opportunities, the skills required and the CET courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: We should roll out an online SkillsFuture Career Guidance tool to help individuals assess their own competencies and credentials against skills required in job vacancies in growth clusters, and direct them to relevant CET courses to develop proficiency in the required competencies.

sections.label: Work-Study as mainstream pathway
sections.summary: The speaker supports Work-Study programmes and welcomes the goal of making them a mainstream pathway for 12% of each cohort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: I have been a strong proponent of Work-Study programmes as they can be very effective in preparing our students to be job-ready in the world of work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: I am also heartened, like Dr Intan Mokhtar, to hear the ambitious goal to make this a mainstream pathway, with the declared ambition of 12% of each cohort.

sections.label: PSEA balances and gig workers
sections.summary: MOE said about 90% of PSEA balances went to CPF over three years, and a survey found gig workers seeking other jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOE confirmed in January that over the past three years, about 90% of PSEA accounts had balances transferred to CPF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It seems a waste to channel the balances for housing and retirement when its primary purpose was post-secondary education when the account holder is young.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope MOE will, at least, look at case-by-case applications and appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: In a survey reported in the Straits Times last November, nine in 10 full-time gig workers were looking for other jobs, and six in 10 were undergoing training or skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Seven in 10 were worried about losing their gig jobs.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-ups and courses
sections.summary: The speaker praises course range and SkillsFuture Credit top-ups and asks if those aged 40 to 60 could use credits before 1 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The range of courses is impressive, from languages to healthcare, culinary skills to information technology and more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I appreciate the $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up for Singaporeans aged 25 and above and the additional one-off SkillsFuture Credit of $500 for every citizen aged 40 to 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider allowing this group to utilise their SkillsFuture Credits earlier, before the commencement date of 1 October this year?

sections.label: Course standards and fraudulent credits
sections.summary: The speaker asks what measures the Ministry has to ensure course content and teaching standards and prevent fraudulent use of SkillsFuture Credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What measures does the Ministry have to ensure that the content and teaching standards of the courses are of a high standard and to prevent fraudulent use of SkillsFuture Credits?

sections.label: Social impact bonds launched
sections.summary: By one estimate, as of July 2019, 132 SIBs were launched in 25 countries, raising over $420 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: By one estimate, as of July 2019, 132 SIBs have been launched in 25 countries, raising more than $420 million in investment to address social challenges.

sections.label: Singapore workforce skills rankings
sections.summary: The 2019 World Economic Forum report ranks Singapore third for current workforce skillsets and 28th for future workforce skillsets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in the global competitiveness report by the World Economic Forum in 2019, Singapore is ranked third for skillsets of the current workforce but 28th for the skillsets of the future workforce.

sections.label: Reskilling needs and course access
sections.summary: Employers estimated by 2022 over 54% of employees need reskilling, and the speaker asks about awareness and access to courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the latest future of job study by the World Economic Forum, employers surveyed estimated that by 2022, no less than 54% of all employees will require significant reskilling and upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of this, 10% will require additional skills training of more than a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While we have IHLs which have already have in-depth curriculum available for skills in these new industries, what are the Ministry's plans to raise awareness of existing curriculum and to make these courses more accessible to companies and the workforce, and how can trade associations and chambers play a role in this?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package
sections.summary: The speaker supports the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package, calling it a welcomed initiative for 40 to 60-year-old workers to upskill, transition and stay employed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: I stand in support of the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: This is a much-welcomed initiative to support our 40 to 60-year-old workers to upskill, transition to new careers and stay employed.

sections.label: Train-and-Place programme suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Ministry consider a Train-and-Place programme to complement the approach and more comprehensively support workers' reskilling and career transition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Given the goal of doubling the number of job placements of workers in their 40s and 50s, I would like to suggest to the Ministry to consider complementing this approach with a Train-and-Place programme instead to more comprehensively support reskilling and career transition of the workers.

sections.label: School-based after-school care waitlist
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for an update on the average waitlist for school-based after-school care and urges MOE to increase capacity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Can the Minister give the House an update on what is the average waitlist for school-based after-school care service?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: I urge MOE to consider to increase the capacity of school-based after-school care service to cater for at least 50% of the Primary 1, Primary 2 and Primary 3 cohorts in each primary school.

sections.label: Scaling up career transition programmes
sections.summary: The speaker asks what efforts are being taken to scale up career transition programmes for mid-career switchers, given a target to double annual job placements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: While a target has been set to double the annual job placement of those in their 40s and 50s to around 5,500 by 2025, what efforts are being taken to scale up career transition programmes for mid-career switchers?

sections.label: Increasing reskilling programme capacity
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOE to consider increasing capacity of reskilling programmes such as PCP, CET centre career transition programmes and sector-specific programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: For a start, I would like MOE to consider increasing the capacity of reskilling programmes, such as PCP under the Adapt and Grow initiative, career transition programmes delivered by the CET centres and those offered by sector-specific programmes.

sections.label: Teacher verbal abuse and humiliation
sections.summary: The passage describes teachers calling students stupid, throwing homework in the trash, flashing wrong answers, yelling and blaming students in front of classmates.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Being called bodoh, stupid or 笨蛋 by your teacher, having your teacher throw your homework into the trash in full view of your classmates, seeing your name and wrong test answers flashed on the screen for the entire class to see, having your teacher tell you loudly and harshly in front of everyone that you will never amount to anything, being screamed and yelled at for giving wrong or incomplete answers, enduring blame from your classmates for depriving everyone of your teacher's promised treat because you failed to score the minimum grade like everyone else.

sections.label: Teacher aggressions affect students
sections.summary: Many teachers go the extra mile, but parents and students report a minority commit aggressions impacting students' well-being and motivation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, many are role models who go the extra mile for students in need, encouraging and inspiring our students.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I have received considerable feedback from parents and students that a minority do commit such aggressions that, while seemingly minor, nevertheless, have considerable impact on our students' well-being and motivation to learn.

sections.label: Psychological safety in classrooms
sections.summary: With students topping for fear of failure, psychological safety in classrooms needs closer attention and investment.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of our students coming in tops for fear of failure, psychological safety in our classrooms is something we must pay closer attention to and invest in.

sections.label: Teacher training, principals, counsellor ratio
sections.summary: Speaker asks Ministry about equipping teachers for socio-emotional teaching, educating principals on intervening with such teachers, and notes a counsellor-student ratio of about one to 800.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I had mentioned in my Adjournment Motion on the fear of failure, that we must make our schools feel like safe spaces in which to fail, and to try again.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask the Ministry what efforts have been made to equip our teachers for the socio-emotional aspects of teaching.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Parents have also shared that when they provide feedback on such aggressions to the school leadership, the teachers are excused for being "old school" and that their approach should thus be tolerated.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask what more we can do to educate our school principals on recognising the harms of such aggressions and how they can effectively intervene to manage such teachers?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on the data provided to a Parliamentary Question on counsellors, I estimate the counsellor-student ratio to be approximately one is to 800, which seems to pale in comparison with some Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) education systems.

sections.label: Mental health consultation on counselling
sections.summary: Thirty-five percent of respondents from the speaker's team's public consultation on mental health cited quality in school counselling as a key concern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirty-five percent of respondents from the public consultation on mental health that my team and I did mentioned quality in school counselling as a key concern.

sections.label: Depression affects Singapore youths
sections.summary: MOH reported that studies in Singapore suggest depression alone affects up to 18% of youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOH reported that studies in Singapore suggest depression alone affects up to 18% of youths.

sections.label: Financial assistance for education
sections.summary: Financial assistance aims to ensure no child is denied a good education due to family finances, and the speaker is heartened by enhanced MOE schemes and bursaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: A key approach to this is by offering financial assistance to ensure no child will be denied of a good education due to the family’s financial situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Hence, I am heartened at the announcements to enhance MOE Financial Assistance Scheme and bursaries for higher education.

sections.label: Edusave awards for madrasah students
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOE to extend Edusave Awards and financial assistance to Singaporean full-time madrasah students, noting benefits exclude foreign-passport students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: The Prime Minister mentioned, "This is a signal that we value every child and we help with a sense of solidarity among the next generation." Sir, on the very basis of valuing every child and a sense of solidarity as mentioned the Prime Minister, MOE should consider to extend Edusave Awards and its Financial Assistance Scheme to Singaporean full-time madrasah students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: In addition, they also receive free textbooks and uniforms as well as some pocket money.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: However, these benefits do not apply to students with foreign passports, even if one of their parents or legal guardians is a Singaporean Citizen or Permanent Resident.

sections.label: University tuition fee increases
sections.summary: The passage states local undergraduate fee hikes ranged from 0.6% to 8%, costs rose 38% since 2007, and all six local universities raised fees in August 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: At universities, the fee hikes for local undergraduates for previous years have ranged from 0.6% to 8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: CNBC estimated that Singapore university costs have risen 38% since 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Most recently, in August 2018, all six local universities have raised tuition fees.

sections.label: Enhanced bursaries for ITE students
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes enhanced Government bursaries for ITE students and asks MOE for details, beneficiary numbers and how to apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Through these and other measures, we have raised the standard of ITE graduates, many of whom contribute meaningfully to our country and economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I welcome the enhancements to the Government bursaries for ITE students as announced in the Budget Statement and would like to ask if MOE can share more details on the enhanced support, including the expected number of students who will benefit from this enhancement and how they can apply for it.

sections.label: No local music in syllabus
sections.summary: The passage states the existing music syllabus has no mention or teaching of Singaporean compositions, local composers, musicians and artistes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From the existing music syllabus, there is currently no mention and teaching of Singaporean compositions, local composers, musicians and artistes in the music curriculum.

sections.label: Arts visits and artist involvement
sections.summary: The speaker proposes MOE let students visit national arts companies and shows, and involve artists and musicians in curriculum planning and dialogue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Teachers and students should step out to indulge in the atmospheres of the arts at the different locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose for MOE to consider: one, allowing our students to pay visits to national arts companies, watch theatre shows, musical performances and even concerts, and arts groups and companies can host these students on one-hour learning journeys; two, involving artists and musicians in curriculum planning and allowing them to have dialogue sessions and conversations with the community and arts sector to build a robust curriculum.

sections.label: Local arts in curriculum
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOE includes more local arts resources in music and art curriculum and invites Cultural Medallion and Young Artist Award recipients to share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In order to develop local artistic talents, we should promote local arts through education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope MOE will consider including more local arts resources in the planning of music and art curriculum in schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also hope MOE will consider inviting past recipients of the Cultural Medallion and Young Artist Award to share their creative journeys and experiences.

sections.label: Aspiration for Arts University
sections.summary: The speaker believes Singapore, as an aspiring Arts Nation, should have its own Arts University.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As an aspiring Arts Nation, I believe that we should have our own Arts University.

sections.label: Jurong Central Student Assistance Scheme
sections.summary: The scheme started two years ago helps students from families receiving Social Service Office financial assistance, giving $40 to $50 monthly vouchers with parental consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Two years ago, we started the Jurong Central Student Assistance Scheme or SAS, that helps students from families that receive financial assistance from the Social Service Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We provide $40 to $50 vouchers per month for each student when they to join SAS with parental consent.

sections.label: Scheme Beneficiaries and Donors
sections.summary: 50 students from over 30 families benefited over 20 months, and two donors gave more than $250,000 over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To-date, 50 students from more than 30 families have benefited from the scheme for the last 20 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have managed to get two donors to donate more than $250,000 over five years.

sections.label: UPLIFT Progress and Banding
sections.summary: Over a year after UPLIFT was announced, the speaker asks MOE for a progress update, noting Full Subject-based Banding implementation by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As more than a year has passed since UPLIFT was first announced, I would like to ask MOE for the progress update.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, last year, the Ministry announced major structural changes to the education system, including the implementation of Full Subject-based Banding in our Secondary schools by 2024.

sections.label: School-Home Co-operation Guidelines
sections.summary: Guidelines for meaningful school-home co-operation were released last year so parents and schools can work together on children's development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Last year, a set of guidelines for meaningful school-home co-operation was released, so parents and schools can work together to enhance children's development.

sections.label: Partnerships for Student Development
sections.summary: ITE graduates got upgrading opportunities and disadvantaged students got support, and the speaker asks how MOE will build partnerships with parents, industry and community.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: For example, last year, they built up upgrading opportunities for our ITE graduates.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: There is also enhanced support for disadvantaged students through community partnerships and after-school support.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Looking ahead, how does MOE intend to build strong partnerships with parents, industry partners and the community to develop the values, dispositions and skills that will place our students in good stead for the future?

sections.label: PSLE scoring system changes
sections.summary: PSLE students will be graded in wider bands called Achievement Levels instead of fine T-scores.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: A major move is the changes we are making to the PSLE scoring system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will grade students in wider bands, what we call Achievement Levels, as opposed to differentiating them very finely through today's T-scores.

sections.label: Simulated secondary school cut-off points
sections.summary: Simulated cut-off points under the new PSLE scoring system for selected Secondary schools will be released later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Sometime later this year, we will release simulated cut-off points under the new PSLE scoring system for selected Secondary schools.

sections.label: Removal of school exams
sections.summary: Primary 1 and 2 exams are removed, and many Primary 3, 5 and Secondary 3 mid-year exams are being removed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: All Primary schools have removed exams for Primary 1 and 2.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This year, 60% of Primary schools would have no Primary 3 and 5 mid-year exams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As for Secondary schools, all have removed Secondary 1 mid-year exams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This year, more than 90% will be removing Secondary 3 mid-year exams.

sections.label: Full Subject-Based Banding pilot
sections.summary: Secondary school streaming is phased out by 2024, replaced by Full SBB, piloted this year in 28 schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At last year’s Committee of Supply debate, I announced the phasing out of Secondary school streaming by 2024 and replaced it with Full Subject-Based Banding or Full SBB.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As Members know, this year, 28 Secondary schools are piloting Full SBB.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Of all the Secondary 2 students who are offered this option, more than two-thirds took it up, and that is encouraging.

sections.label: Nationwide Full SBB rollout
sections.summary: Lessons will be drawn from pilot schools to roll out Full SBB nationwide by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Important social dynamics are changing in these schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will learn from the experiences of the pilot schools and roll out Full SBB nationwide by 2024.

sections.label: Tertiary education bursary increase
sections.summary: Tertiary education bursaries for lower income groups were increased, lowering annual course fees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is why at the National Day Rally last year, the Prime Minister announced a significant increase in tertiary education bursary quanta for lower income groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, for a student from the lowest income group, he pays $150 in annual course fees in Polytechnic, and $2,000 in annual course fees for a general degree in the Autonomous Universities.

sections.label: Mother Tongue and Language Elective Programmes
sections.summary: A Mother Tongue Support Programme for Primary 3 and 4 students will be fully rolled out in 2021, and a Language Elective Programme was introduced in 15 Secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In Primary schools, we introduced a Mother Tongue Support Programme for Primary 3 and 4 students who have a weak command of MTL.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Last year, 60 pilot schools enlisted 1,100 students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It will be fully rolled out to all schools in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For students who are strong in MTL, we introduced the Language Elective Programme (LEP) in 15 Secondary schools this year.

sections.label: Updating CCE curriculum
sections.summary: The CCE curriculum will be updated and strengthened with five changes, the first being restructured formal CCE lessons to reinforce teaching of moral values.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We need to update the CCE curriculum to reflect this imperative and reinforce the teaching of values in our children from as young an age as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, we will build on the existing CCE curriculum and strengthen it with the following five changes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Number one, we will restructure formal CCE lessons to reinforce the teaching of moral values.

sections.label: Emphasis on cyber wellness
sections.summary: The second change places more emphasis on cyber wellness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The second change, we will place more emphasis on cyber wellness.

sections.label: Focus on mental wellness
sections.summary: The third change gives the CCE curriculum greater focus on mental wellness, which is closely related to cyber wellness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The third change, the CCE curriculum will have greater focus on mental wellness, which is closely related to cyber wellness.

sections.label: Progressive implementation from 2021
sections.summary: The new CCE curriculum will be progressively implemented from 2021 in all Primary and Secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The new CCE curriculum will be progressively implemented from 2021 in all Primary and Secondary schools.

sections.label: Deeper appreciation of regional countries
sections.summary: As a start, this will be done in three ways, and it must provide students with a deeper appreciation of the geographies, histories, cultures, languages and economies of regional countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As a start, we will do this in three ways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It must provide students with a deeper appreciation of the geographies, histories, cultures, languages and economies of our regional countries.

sections.label: 70-70 overseas stint aspiration
sections.summary: The aspiration is for 70% of IHL students to have an overseas stint, with 70% of that going to ASEAN, China or India.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng in the Budget Statement, our aspiration is "70-70".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This means to have 70% of IHL students undergo an overseas stint and with 70% of that going to ASEAN, China or India.

sections.label: Conversational Malay and Chinese offerings
sections.summary: About 60% of Primary schools and 40% of Secondary schools offer Conversational Malay and Chinese.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, about 60% of Primary schools and 40% of Secondary schools offer Conversational Malay and Chinese.

sections.label: MOE framework and digital literacy
sections.summary: MOE's framework is find, think, apply and create, and MOE will launch a National Digital Literacy Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The framework MOE has adopted is: find, think, apply and create.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Recognising the importance of digital literacy, MOE will launch a National Digital Literacy Programme (NDLP).

sections.label: Computational thinking in existing subjects
sections.summary: Computational thinking elements are present in existing subjects, especially Mathematics, so no new subject is needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: These are skills largely found in what we call computational thinking.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But we do not need a new subject called computational thinking.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The elements are present in existing subjects, especially Mathematics, where there is a strong focus on problem solving already.

sections.label: Singapore Student Learning Space initiative
sections.summary: The Singapore Student Learning Space holds almost the whole curriculum with animation, interactives, videos, assessments and other resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: A major initiative in this area is the Singapore Student Learning Space (SLS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Almost the whole of our curriculum is on SLS, complete with animation, interactives, videos, assessments and other resources.

sections.label: Pilot project using SLS
sections.summary: Eight schools started a pilot where teachers used SLS and every student got a personal learning device, yielding many lessons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Then students are more likely to internalise the lessons and achieve better education outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, we got eight schools to start a pilot project where teachers conducted lessons using SLS and gave every student a personal learning device to access the SLS portal and we learned many things from this pilot project.

sections.label: Devices for Secondary students
sections.summary: By 2024 every school will have e-pedagogy capabilities and every Secondary 1 student a personal learning device, and by 2028 all Secondary students will have a digital device.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By 2024, we will equip every school with e-pedagogy capabilities and every single Secondary 1 student with a personal learning device.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: By 2028, all Secondary school students will be equipped with a digital device and this will address the concerns of Ms Denise Phua and Dr Intan.

sections.label: Edusave top-ups for students
sections.summary: A $150 Bicentennial Bonus top-up was provided, and another $200 top-up will go to Edusave accounts of Primary and Secondary Singaporean students, with subsidies ensuring $0 out-of-pocket cost for lower income groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We also provided a $150 Bicentennial Bonus top-up for all Primary and Secondary Singaporean students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This year, and in anticipation of the full roll-out of this initiative, we will provide another $200 top-up to the Edusave accounts of all Singaporean students in Primary and Secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Some who have used more of their Edusave funds might have to fork out a bit of cash.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But MOE will provide further subsidies for students from lower income household groups and ensure that their out-of-pocket cost is $0.

sections.label: ICT student intake
sections.summary: They now take in a total of 2,800 ICT students a year, almost three times more than before.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, they are taking in a total of 2,800 ICT students a year, almost three times more than before.

sections.label: Mdm Lee on teaching technology
sections.summary: Mdm Lee told Senior Minister of State Chee that technology will not replace teachers, but teachers who know how to use technology will replace those who do not.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It turns out Mdm Lee is a firm believer in using technology to teach languages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: She told Senior Minister of State Chee that technology will not replace teachers, but teachers who know how to use technology will replace those who do not know how to use technology.

sections.label: Teacher professional autonomy
sections.summary: Professional development and teaching duties are not a zero-sum game, and teachers should decide for themselves what training they need, which is the essence of professional autonomy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They do not see professional development and teaching duties as a zero-sum game.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But to make sure that the training is useful, it is important that teachers decide for themselves what kind of training they need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is the essence of professional autonomy – teachers taking ownership of the tools of their craft.

sections.label: SkillsFuture for Educators name
sections.summary: Professional ownership is a core philosophy of SkillsFuture, and MOE named its initiative to upgrade teachers' skills "SkillsFuture for Educators".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The concept of professional ownership applies to all industries, trades and crafts and, in fact, this is a core philosophy of SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, in MOE, when we were thinking how do we name this significant initiative to upgrade the skills of our teaches, we came up with the name "SkillsFuture for Educators".

sections.label: Bilingualism and structural education changes
sections.summary: Bilingualism is the cornerstone, while structural changes nurture joy of learning and replace streaming with Full SBB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second, the roots represent the cornerstone of our education system which is bilingualism and learning languages for life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Then, the stem and the branches represent significant structural changes that we are making – the first structural change is to nurture the joy of learning, by making changes to the PSLE scoring system, reducing examination load.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The second structural change is to phase out streaming and replace it with Full SBB.

sections.label: Learn for Life movement
sections.summary: Six thrusts form the Learn for Life movement, guiding efforts to raise school education over five to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Together, these six thrusts form the "Learn for Life" movement for schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It will guide our efforts to raise the school education system to a new level, in the next five to 10 years.

sections.label: Lifting the bottom approach
sections.summary: The approach is not to cap the top but lift the bottom, extending help to students needing assistance most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To tackle these challenges, we should not penalise the schools or the individuals who have done well, for which parent does not want their child to do well and to be the best they can be?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is why our approach is "not to cap the top, but lift the bottom", extend more help to students who need assistance most, devote resources and implement programmes that lift the quality, standards and experience across the board.

sections.label: National system of quality
sections.summary: Singapore delivers high quality national systems, and education must remain a work in progress with low school fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In Singapore, we counter this trend by ensuring that whether it is in healthcare, transport, public housing or education, we deliver a national system of high quality, even world-class quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And that is why the education system must always be a work in progress, always be honest in identifying our strengths as well as our gaps and areas for improvement, keep engaging and working with stakeholders to improve it, and doing all these while keeping school fees to a few dollars a month for the great majority of our schools.

sections.label: Supporting student well-being
sections.summary: Many colleagues asked how to better support students' well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Many colleagues have asked how we can better support our students’ well-being.

sections.label: Teacher conduct and student resilience
sections.summary: Schools intervene in unprofessional teacher conduct, and help students develop the resilience mindset 'I am, I have, I can'.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: There are times where teachers have to be more strict with students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, in cases of unprofessional conduct, where the teachers step over the bounds, such as deliberate attacks on students’ self-esteem, schools will take a serious view, and intervene as necessary to safeguard our students’ well-being, and maintain a positive learning environment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To help students face challenges confidently, we will help students develop the resilience mindset of "I am, I have, I can". "I am" is about helping students to appreciate their strengths and harness positive beliefs about themselves. "I have" is about enabling students to tap into their social and emotional resources, like peer and family support.

sections.label: Peer support in schools
sections.summary: Peer support structures will be established in every school by 2022, strengthening the peer support culture.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: That is what makes peer support so powerful.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will establish peer support structures in every school by 2022 and continue to strengthen the peer support culture in our schools.

sections.label: Mental health education in CCE
sections.summary: Mental health education will be included in the Secondary CCE curriculum to help students understand mental health issues and seek help.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In addition to this, we will include mental health education in the CCE curriculum for Secondary schools,	to	help	students	to understand common mental health issues and their symptoms, know when and how to seek help for themselves and others, and develop empathy and care towards persons with mental health issues.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The new mental health education in schools will complement our earlier efforts to help our students develop a resilience mindset and to foster peer support cultures.

sections.label: External mental health professionals

sentences.text: External professionals include the hospitals’ REACH teams – that is Response, Early Intervention and Assessment in Community mental Health – and IMH's Community Health Assessment Team (CHAT).

sections.label: Youth Mental Well-Being Network
sections.summary: A new Youth Mental Well-Being Network will bring together more than 700 people who responded to the open call.

sentences.text: Last week, Minster Desmond announced that we will set up a new Youth Mental Well-Being Network, bringing together more than 700 people who responded to the open call, many of whom are passionate youths.

sections.label: SPED school funding increase

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: MOE’s funding for SPED schools has increased by about 40% in the last five years.

sections.label: SPED students aged 18

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Of the 422 SPED students aged 18 years old in 2019, 150 remain in their schools this year, when they turn 19.

sections.label: SEN Fund disbursements
sections.summary: The SEN Fund has helped students keep up with academic learning and improve interaction with peers, with about $675,000 disbursed to over 120 students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It has helped students to keep up with academic learning and improve day-to-day interaction with peers.

sections.label: SEN Fund extension

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These students will be able to tap on the SEN Fund to purchase assistive technology devices, up to a cap of $5,000, from 1 April 2020.

sections.label: Financial assistance beneficiaries 2019
