sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2019, 52,000 students from lower income families at the Primary to pre-University levels benefited from the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS), SPED Financial Assistance and the Independent School Bursary.

sections.label: Transport and meal subsidies
sections.summary: From April 2020, public transport subsidy rises from $10 to $15 monthly, school bus subsidy to 60% from 50%, and Secondary school meal subsidy to $2.90 from $2.50.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Recognising increased transport costs, from April 2020, we will raise the public transport subsidy from $10 to $15 per month, for Primary up to pre-University levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For Primary school students who take the school bus, we will also enhance the school bus transport subsidy to 60% of monthly payable fees, up from 50% today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Next, we will enhance the school meal subsidies for Secondary school students from April 2020 to $2.90 per school meal, up from $2.50 today.

sections.label: Fee subsidy and bursary
sections.summary: From April 2020, students from low-income families will also receive a full fee subsidy and an enhanced cash bursary of $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Beyond this, from April 2020, students from low-income families will also benefit from a full fee subsidy, in addition to an enhanced cash bursary of $1,500.

sections.label: SCCs in all primary schools
sections.summary: MOE achieved its target of opening a Student Care Centre in all 185 primary schools this year, up from 170 last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Last year, I said MOE would expand our current provisions for after-school support, so I am very happy to announce that we have achieved our target of opening an SCC in all 185 Primary schools this year, up from 170 last year.

sections.label: Student care fee subsidies
sections.summary: Children from low-income families in MSF-registered SCCs receive ComCare SCFA subsidies, but some MOE FAS students still pay over $120 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Today, children from low-income families attending MSF-registered SCCs receive fee subsidies under the ComCare Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA) scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, some students on MOE's FAS still pay more than $120 per month after SCFA subsidies.

sections.label: SCC pilot enrolment
sections.summary: Tours and parent induction sessions were held, and 87 of 100 identified students were enrolled in the pilot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They conducted tours of the SCC for the students and induction sessions for parents, because we want to get the parents on-board to make sure the parents send their children to the SCCs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And I am most heartened to announce that we successfully enrolled 87 of the 100 students that we identified for the pilot.

sections.label: Enhanced outreach in all schools
sections.summary: MOE will implement the enhanced outreach approach in all primary schools given positive outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Given the positive outcomes such as these, MOE will be implementing this enhanced outreach approach in all Primary schools.

sections.label: Reading with You programme
sections.summary: CMG worked with New Town Primary School and Qihua Primary School to start a Chinese reading programme called Reading with You.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Last year, CMG worked with New Town Primary school and Qihua Primary School to start a Chinese reading programme called "Reading with You".

sections.label: GEAR-UP secondary school programmes
sections.summary: After-school GEAR-UP programmes run in over 70 secondary schools for more than 3,000 students, scaling to 120 schools this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: At the Secondary school level, we have set up after-school programmes in over 70 schools under GEAR-UP, benefiting more than 3,000 students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These programmes focus on befriending and mentoring by trusted adults, peer support and interest-based activities to engage the students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are on track to scale up GEAR-UP to 120 Secondary schools this year.

sections.label: Town-Level Coordinator role
sections.summary: The Town-Level Coordinator will help integrate school-based and community-based support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Town-Level Coordinator will help integrate school-based and community-based support.

sections.label: UPLIFT Community Pilot
sections.summary: The UPLIFT Community Pilot pools schools' and community's wisdom and resources to support vulnerable families, with over 300 students estimated to benefit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The UPLIFT Community Pilot will pool together the collective wisdom and resources of schools and the community, to better support vulnerable families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We estimate that more than 300 students could benefit from this pilot.

sections.label: SkillsFuture beneficiaries
sections.summary: About 500,000 individuals and 14,000 enterprises have benefited from SkillsFuture initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: About 500,000 individuals and 14,000 enterprises have benefited from SkillsFuture initiatives.

sections.label: Anchor enterprise training partnerships
sections.summary: Partnerships with intermediaries like trade associations, anchor enterprises and professional firms will be used, working with SkillsFuture Queen Bee companies to drive enterprise-led training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is where partnerships with intermediaries, such as trade associations, anchor enterprises and professional firms, can come in handy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will work with a group of large anchor enterprises – also known as SkillsFuture Queen Bee companies – to drive enterprise-led training.

sections.label: SME training and credit
sections.summary: Over five years, up to 40 anchor enterprises will partner to reach 4,000 companies, especially SMEs, which can tap a $10,000 SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Over the next five years, we aim to partner up to 40 anchor	enterprises	to	reach	out	to	4,000	companies, especially SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To further support their transformation efforts, SMEs can tap on the $10,000 SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Series and Frameworks
sections.summary: SSG worked with IHLs on SkillsFuture Series courses and 34 Skills Frameworks, and with PwC, INSEAD and SMU on Masterclasses benefiting around 100 individuals this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: SSG has worked with the IHLs to curate the SkillsFuture Series courses focusing on such skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: There are 34 Skills Frameworks which employers can use to plan their talent pipeline for emerging and future jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, SSG has worked with PwC Singapore and Universities like INSEAD and SMU to launch a number of Masterclasses for SME business leaders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: These will benefit around 100 individuals this year.

sections.label: Enterprises workplace learning goal
sections.summary: By 2025, the aim is to help over 1,200 enterprises build workplace learning and work-study best practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: By 2025, we aim to help over 1,200 enterprises build best practices in workplace learning and work-study capabilities.

sections.label: Work-Study Programme expansion
sections.summary: Work-Study Programmes will expand to 12% of each age cohort by 2025, about 5,000 intake places, up from 3.5% or 1,600.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: About 5,500 students have benefited from Work-Study Programmes since their launch in 2015 and about 1,400 companies have participated so far.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will expand the SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes into a mainstream pathway in the Next Bound of SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We aim to offer this pathway to 12% of each age cohort by 2025, and this translates to about 5,000 intake places, which is an increase from the current 3.5% or 1,600 places.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up
sections.summary: A $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up will be provided to every Singaporean aged 25 and above this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: More than 90% of SkillsFuture Credit claims were for work- related and industry-oriented courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will provide a top-up of $500 to the SkillsFuture Credit for every Singaporean aged 25 and above this year.

sections.label: SEP Training Support Scheme
sections.summary: MOM announced the SEP Training Support Scheme, giving self-employed persons a training allowance over three months for SkillsFuture series courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Yesterday, MOM announced the new SEP Training Support Scheme, where all self-employed persons will be provided with a training allowance over the next three months when they attend courses under the SkillsFuture series and selected sector-specific training programmes.

sections.label: Mid-Career Support Credit top-up
sections.summary: A worker aged 40 to 60 this year will receive a total SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $1,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our aim is to double the numbers in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will also provide an additional $500 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career Support).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In other words, a worker aged 40 to 60 this year will receive a total SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $1,000.

sections.label: Next Bound SkillsFuture spending
sections.summary: Over the next five years, Government will spend about $1.4 billion on the Next Bound of SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Over the next five years, Government will spend about $1.4 billion on the Next Bound of SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Phasing out SkillsFuture Qualification Awards
sections.summary: Schemes that have become less relevant over time, such as the SkillsFuture Qualification Awards, will be gradually phased out.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Schemes that have become less relevant over time, such as the SkillsFuture Qualification Awards, will be gradually phased out.

sections.label: Course fee subsidy and Absentee Payroll
sections.summary: Course fee subsidy was increased to a flat 90% and Absentee Payroll rates raised to $10 per hour for tourism and air transport sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: One recent change that we made was to increase the course fee subsidy to a flat rate of 90% and raise the Absentee Payroll rates to $10 per hour for sectors like tourism and air transport, which are worst-hit by the drop in tourist arrivals.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-ups and Work-Study
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Credit top-ups of $500, plus $500 mid-career support, and Work-Study Programmes expanded to 12% of each cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: One of the key initiatives in the Next Bound of SkillsFuture is to enhance support for individuals to pursue lifelong learning through a SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500 for every Singaporean aged 25 and above this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In addition, Singaporean mid-career workers aged 40 to 60 in 2020 will receive an additional SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career Support) of $500 for them to access Career Transition Programmes, as part of the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This group of workers will receive a total of $1,000 in SkillsFuture Credit top-ups.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will also be growing the SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes into a mainstream pathway which will be made available to 12% of each cohort.

sections.label: Two-year Polytechnic diploma courses
sections.summary: For a third of Polytechnic diploma courses, students can graduate with a diploma in two years instead of three.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For a third of the Polytechnic diploma courses, they will be able to graduate with a diploma in two years instead of three years.

sections.label: Guidelines for School-Home Partnerships
sections.summary: The Guidelines for School-Home Partnerships were well received, with teacher-parent conversations shifting from academic achievement to well-being and behaviour.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Our Guidelines for School-Home Partnerships, which were released last year, were well received by parents and schools, and we have observed some encouraging signs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For example, the focus of conversations between teachers and parents has shifted from an overemphasis on academic achievement, to students’ learning dispositions, physical and mental well-being, and classroom behaviour.

sections.label: Music syllabi cultural appreciation
sections.summary: MOE's Music syllabi aim for students to appreciate music across cultures, introducing traditional and contemporary Singapore music and instruments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: One of MOE's key learning objectives of the Music syllabi is for students to appreciate music across local and global cultures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: During music lessons, our students are introduced to traditional and contemporary music and instruments in Singapore through a selection of songs that reflects Singapore's diverse and rich culture.

sections.label: Arts university plan study
sections.summary: MOE and MCCY will continue to study plans to develop local arts institutions, including an arts university suggestion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MOE and MCCY will continue to closely study plans to develop our local arts institutions, including Mr Ho's suggestion of an arts university, taking into account the evolving arts education landscape and developments in the industry.

sections.label: Primary school education subsidies
sections.summary: All primary school students benefit from education subsidies, with some differentiation in subsidy amount reflecting citizenship benefits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: All students in our Primary schools benefit from education subsidies, with some differentiation in the amount of subsidy to reflect the benefits of citizenship.

sections.label: Edusave contributions for citizens
sections.summary: All Singapore Citizens aged seven to 16, regardless of school, receive an annual Edusave contribution based on age.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: All Singapore Citizens aged seven to 16, regardless of school, receive an annual EC based on their age.

sections.label: Madrasah student support schemes
sections.summary: Private school students are not eligible for the Financial Assistance Scheme or Edusave Awards, so madrasah students receive Edusave Contributions, Madrasah Student Awards and PROMAS assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Students in private schools are hence not eligible for the Financial Assistance Scheme or Edusave Awards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Hence, students in madrasahs receive support through the Edusave Contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: They are also eligible for the Madrasah Student Awards administered by MUIS, which recognise madrasah students' educational excellence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In addition, MUIS provides assistance for madrasah students from low-income families through the Progress Fund Madrasah Assistance Scheme (PROMAS).

sections.label: Mother Tongue Language committee collaboration
sections.summary: MOE has collaborated with the three Mother Tongue Language Learning Promotion Committees since their formation about 15 years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: MOE has collaborated with the three Mother Tongue Language Learning Promotion Committees since their formation some 15 years ago.

sections.label: Creative songwriting category
sections.summary: A new Creative songwriting category was introduced where students submit original compositions based on the secondary school Mother Tongue Language curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Recently, we introduced a new “Creative” songwriting category where students submit original compositions based on the MTL curriculum taught in secondary school.

sections.label: Malay and Tamil language programmes
sections.summary: Perkasa Warisan and NUS and NTU youths run Malay cultural activities and an AI and Tamil Language programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Since 2018, the "Perkasa Warisan" camp has brought together community partners, as Miss Cheng Li Hui mentioned earlier, to provide immersive experiences, specifically tied to the language and also the cultural components of the Malay language curriculum, such as activities on the art of Malay gastronomy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Tech-savvy youths from NUS and also the youths from NTU have made learning Tamil fun for Upper Primary students, through a programme called "Artificial Intelligence and Tamil Language".

sections.label: Climate change in curriculum
sections.summary: Climate change is integrated across subjects at different levels of the national curriculum to foster active citizenship.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This includes, as Miss Cheng Li Hui suggested, engaging our youths in current issues, like climate change to foster in them traits of active citizenship and a shared concern for Singapore and the world.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We currently integrate the topic of climate change across various subjects at different levels of the national curriculum.

sections.label: Junior Environmental Ambassadors training
sections.summary: Students are trained as Junior Environmental Ambassadors in the Green Schools programme by South West CDC and NEA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: For instance, students are trained to become "Junior Environmental Ambassadors" in the Green Schools programme by the South West Community Development Council (South West CDC) and NEA.

sections.label: Student ambassadors and CCA pilots
sections.summary: Nearly 300 ambassadors from 49 schools championed green initiatives, and CCA selection trials and combined school teams are being piloted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Last year, close to 300 student ambassadors across 49 schools completed their training and went on to champion green initiatives in their schools in the South West district.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Also central to holistic education, is the students' participation in co-curricular activities (CCAs), which allow them to discover their interest and talents, forge friendships with peers of diverse backgrounds, as well as develop character and resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We are glad that Miss Cheng Li Hui supports our initiative to pilot the removal of CCA selection trials to help our students develop their passions, regardless of their prior experiences and backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Currently, we are piloting combined teams where two schools run a CCA programme together, and where appropriate, send a combined team to participate in the National School Games (NSG) or Singapore Youth Festival Arts Presentation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As students work together towards a common purpose, there will be plenty of opportunities for them to learn, to appreciate differences, to pick up skills like relationship management.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We are starting this with five pairs of schools.

sections.label: SEN Fund amount questions
sections.summary: The SEN Fund for IHLs was extended to Dyslexia, ADHD and ASD at $5,000, unlike $25,000 for hearing and visual impairment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Would Minister consider all of that, and also maybe add an element of innovation in the graphic so that we could consider for example, schools that may not have to go through the PSLE or a Parent Academy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I think it is great news that the SEN Fund for IHLs has been extended to those who not just have physical disabilities, but also to those with Dyslexia, ADHD and ASD.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: But the amount given is $5,000, if I heard correctly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: In the actual original fund, there is $25,000 for those with hearing and visual impairment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I was wondering why the extension is for $5,000, and not $25,000, why not in between?

sections.label: Extending special school years
sections.summary: An appeal is made to let all SPED students stay in special schools until age 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: My last question is an appeal to extend the special school years for all of the SPED students – not just those who are currently allowed to study until 21, but for all of them to be able to stay until the age 21.

sections.label: SEN Fund payout amounts
sections.summary: The SEN Fund lets eligible students with physical impairment tap up to $5,000, and those with visual or hearing loss up to $25,000, as their expenses are higher.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Currently, under the SEN Fund, eligible students with physical impairment can tap up to $5,000 on the SEN Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Eligible students with visual or hearing loss can tap up to $25,000 and that is because for those with visual or hearing loss, the expenses are higher for them in terms of the assistive devices, that is one; as well as the services.

sections.label: SEN Fund extension to learning needs
sections.summary: The SEN Fund has just been extended to students with learning and behavioural needs, and this is just a start.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Do not forget, we have just extended the SEN Fund to students with learning and behavioural needs, and this is just a start.

sections.label: School-to-Work Transition Programme
sections.summary: The School-to-Work Transition Programme in all SPED schools offers customised training and work options, starting in the final school year and continuing a year after graduation with SG Enable support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Number two, we have the School-to-Work Transition Programme in all the SPED schools and that is to offer customised training pathways cum work options for the students, who have diverse disability profiles, who may not benefit from the vocational certification but they are still capable of work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The School-to-Work Transition Programme begins in the student's final year of schooling, when he or she is referred to SG Enable and matched to a suitable employment or training pathway, and the programme continues for one year after he or she graduates, during which he or she is supported by SG Enable.

sections.label: Portal and SkillsFuture Advice guidance
sections.summary: The portal will be enhanced to give recommendations based on an individual's profile and needs, while face-to-face guidance will be provided through SkillsFuture Advice working with career centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The first one, of course, we are going to do it through the portal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the portal will be enhanced to be able to provide some of this information based on the individual's profile, needs, and make some recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But we understand that some Singaporeans will want a more face-to-face interaction, because they are then able to interact with the advisor, they are able to get some guidance to point them in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So that is why we are going to work through the SkillsFuture Advice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But this time round, we will go beyond the community, which is what we have been doing for the past few years, to work with the career centres.

sections.label: Training and employability linkage
sections.summary: There is a need for closer linkage between training and employability, and the quality of training courses has to be curated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The other point that I will just mention briefly is that part of having a closer linkage between training and employability, where we also have to curate the quality of the training courses.

sections.label: Counselling teachers who lose anger
sections.summary: Where teachers cannot control their anger, in the rare occasions it happens, they ought to be counselled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Where teachers cannot control their anger or in the rare occasions that it happens, I think they ought to be counselled.

sections.label: Piloting national device programme
sections.summary: National programmes are piloted first; eight schools piloted showed Wifi dropping and other practical issues, which can be resolved before national rollout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for the second question on the device, these are practical issues we really have to look at on the ground, which is why before we roll out any national programme, we always pilot it first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have piloted in these eight schools and all these issues the Member raised happened, all happened – Wifi kept dropping, all these things happened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But with the experience that we have gained so far, these practical problems can be resolved and we make sure they are resolved before we roll out nationally.

sections.label: Funding for educator training
sections.summary: SkillsFuture for Educators is fully funded, as is training at NIE and the Academy of Singapore Teachers for teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second, our SkillsFuture for Educators is fully funded, just as at NIE, our training at the, Academy of Singapore Teachers (AST), they are fully funded for our teachers.

sections.label: Government funding for education costs
sections.summary: The Government funds over 90% of ITE education costs and about 75% of university costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For the cost of ITE education, we fund over 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And then, for University, the Government funds about 75%.

sections.label: Adjusting fees and bursaries
sections.summary: Fees and bursaries may be adjusted from time to time for cost inflation so education stays affordable, and no one with an IHL place should be denied education due to financial circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: From henceforth, we need to adjust fees from time to time in order to reflect cost inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And bursaries, from time to time, also probably have to adjust, so that education remains affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Our principle is very clear: no one who gains a place in an IHL should be denied of studying, of education, because of financial circumstances.
